$schema_note: VIGIL documented-limitation inventory (W15-1 #393, feeding the W16 burndown). Machine-checked by docs/tests/test_limitation_inventory.py, which runs in the required 'the briefing explains every agent and capability' CI job. JSON, not YAML, on purpose: that job installs only pytest, so PyYAML is unavailable and the guard parses this file with the stdlib json module. Every real-unfinished-code limitation names a code anchor the guard resolves by AST (no import); every re-verified-closed item names an evidence path the guard asserts exists. 'honest_limit_sites' is the code-scan census: the guard scans every non-test product .py for a curated set of honest-limit/deferred debt phrases ('not wired', 'does not yet', 'is a stub', '*-gated', ...) and REFUSES any hit that is neither a VIGIL-LIMIT marker line nor registered here — so adding an unregistered honest-limit docstring turns the build red, and a registered site whose prose is gone turns it red too (bidirectional). See docs/limitations/README.md for the schema, the VIGIL-LIMIT:<id> marker convention, and the thirteen re-verified-closed items listed by name so nobody re-works them.

classes.doc-only: The limitation is a property of the world (hardware absent, no external audit team, a record that can only accrue in the field), not unfinished code. There is nothing to build; the honest state is documented and must not be worded as completeness.
classes.real-unfinished-code: A capability whose software layer is present but deliberately incomplete: a stub that raises, an interface with no runtime, or a path gated on infra/credentials/tooling that is absent here. The anchor names the symbol that carries the honest limit.

severities.critical: Would block a third-party (national-agency) deployment or is a security/safety defect.
severities.high: Materially limits a deployment; a deploying institution must plan around it.
severities.medium: A real gap a careful operator will hit, with a documented fallback.
severities.low: A narrow residual with a working default path; defense-in-depth or quality, not safety.
severities.info: A deliberate, correctly-deferred boundary (hardware/research/external-team). Not debt to burn down; recorded so it is never overclaimed.

dispositions.file-into-w16: An open limitation to be tracked as an issue in the W16 milestone (DECLARED-LIMITATION BURNDOWN). w16_issue carries the issue number once filed, or null while filing is pending owner review.
dispositions.re-verified-closed: Named on an older audit list but re-verified against the current tree as already done. Listed here by name, with the evidence, so no one re-works it.

re_verified_closed.name: Signed governance grants are replayable (promotion + capability latches)
re_verified_closed.summary: The anti-replay pattern was present in one governor file and absent from its two siblings, so a revoked grant was replay-resurrectable. Re-verified closed: the replay guard is now enforced and pinned by a test.

re_verified_closed.name: Engine raw-socket egress sites (CSWSH / race / smuggling) were not software-floored
re_verified_closed.summary: The never-liftable egress floor was wired only on the engine capture paths in #874; the raw sockets in scanner/websocket.py (CSWSH), scanner/race.py::raw_race, and scanner/smuggling.py (raw_send + _desync_leg) still connected on a re-resolved name with no IP floor, so a charter-scoped name resolving or rebinding to metadata/RFC1918 could be dialled. Re-verified closed (WS1.1b, #879): all three now resolve once, run vigil_gateway.denylist.is_egress_denied over every resolved address, refuse metadata/link-local/RFC1918 (and DNS-rebinding), and dial the pinned IP; fail-closed throughout. Channel-only: no FACT minted, _ALL_ORACLES frozen at 15. Proof: scanner/tests/test_{websocket,race,smuggling}.py (floor + anti-rebinding + fail-closed negative controls).

re_verified_closed.summary: There was no backup/restore path for any offense-side state. Re-verified closed: off-host backup and unit-scoped restore ship as vigil backup / vigil restore.

re_verified_closed.name: Audit A12 (#269) — the request-smuggling TIMING mint. Closed; the class itself stays a LEAD
re_verified_closed.summary: SCOPE: what is re-verified closed here is A12's DEFECT — that a bare TIMING anomaly minted a High request_smuggling FACT. That mint is deleted and guarded: scanner.smuggling.detect labels its own result severity Low / 'TIMING LEAD' / UNCONFIRMED, scanner.campaign._smuggling_leads no longer builds any latency FindingContext, and a hanging origin is pinned to produce no finding. NOT CLOSED, and explicitly re-opened by the audit-A red-pen (B1): the Wave-4.2 replacement — a single-connection canary DIFFERENTIAL minting a DIFFERENTIAL_RESPONSE FACT at conf 0.95 — is itself an overclaim, because CWE-444 is two parsers disagreeing and the differential is observed on the one connection VIGIL pipelined the smuggled prefix onto. A benign single origin with no proxy (TE preferred over CL per RFC 9112 6.1, keep-alive pipelining, a stock path-echoing 404) reproduces it, and two ORDINARY pipelined requests with no framing conflict produce the identical canary echo. request_smuggling is therefore LEAD-only on every VIGIL path today; request_smuggling.differential_desync is fact_capable=false with the cross-connection, operator-authorised co-tenant probe named as blocking_work.

limitations.summary: SEV-SNP / TDX attestation providers exist behind the AttestationProvider interface but every method fails closed with NotImplementedError. The SoftwareAttestationProvider proves integrity + origin, never hardware confidentiality; hardware_backed is always False on that path.

limitations.summary: SymbolicCrashRepairTier is a full stub behind the BinaryPatchTier interface; SanitizerSilenceTier proves a fix by oracle silence but its output-based synthesize_patch also raises. The narrow strcpy->strncpy source synthesiser is real; an unrecognised class fabricates no patch.

limitations.summary: SanitizerSilenceTier.synthesize_patch (the output-based synthesis interface) raises NotImplementedError; the tier's value is proving a fix by oracle silence, not generating it.

limitations.summary: Neo4jGraphStore is a real client body, but constructing a LIVE store with no injected driver raises NotImplementedError until the neo4j driver package and a running service are provisioned. EmbeddedGraphStore is the working default.

limitations.title: The pluggable next-gen agent-body is an interface-only scaffold
limitations.summary: AgentBody formalises the think->propose->gate->execute->learn contract (gate-before-execute is structural) but wires no new runtime. The production Strix-based body is one implementation; a next-gen body is not built.

limitations.title: LLM red-team tool live-fire (garak / PyRIT / promptfoo) is tooling-gated
limitations.summary: The external-tool runner is tool-agnostic and live-proven with nmap, but garak/PyRIT/promptfoo are absent from this environment, so their live-fire is deferred and no garak/PyRIT/promptfoo FACT is minted. A new ToolSpec (+ oracle mapping for a non-reachability signal) is all a new tool needs.

limitations.title: Cloud exploitation branches (E1/E2/E3/E5) are fixture-proven, not live-fired
limitations.summary: The IMDS-capture, IAM-escalation, GCP SA-impersonation and secret-validity branches are proven offline over fixtures; no live cloud FACT has been claimed and none exists in the evidence store. Each branch's limitation string in the evidence-branches registry governs admission, so the deferral is enforced, not merely described. Activation needs an operator-provisioned throwaway lab credential.

limitations.title: The offline audit package re-derives EVERY portable (stdlib+cryptography) oracle verdict standalone; only three oracles remain genuinely irreducible (their import-closure needs a non-stdlib module)
limitations.summary: verify_offline.py / docs/proof-carrying-finding/verify_vf.py re-verify authenticity + binding + integrity + chain with no VIGIL runtime AND re-fire (Step 2) every oracle whose body is PURE (import-closure = stdlib + the one Ed25519 lib, cryptography), re-deriving the verdict from the retained oracle_context with nothing installed: the SIX posture oracles (reexecute_posture_oracle), the ACHIEVED_STATE predicate kernel, the GENERAL web-vuln families (reexecute_general_oracle: differential_response (+ smuggling_desync), timing, boolean_inference, side_effect, reflection_context, evaluation (+ ssi), error_signature, sanitizer_signal, system_prompt_disclosure, prompt_injection, sql/command/nosql_injection_breakout, weak_crypto_artifact, prototype_pollution), and — this slice (Lane C/G1) — the former A-prime residual, now ALL ported byte-faithfully: service_reachability, tls_weakness (live-handshake path), active_exposure, dom_execution (+ csp_bypass), credential_stuffing, automated_access/honeypot, jwt_forgery (HS/structural), static_rule, session_fixation, mfa_bypass, password_reset_invariant, csrf_achieved, workflow_abuse, the client-side posture oracles (clickjacking/csrf/postmessage/csp), email_auth/identity posture, certificate_validity (cryptography.x509 DER parse), mobile_posture (cryptography key classification), credential_acceptance, and the WARDEN-gated cloud/cluster capture oracles (imds/secret/gcp/iam/k8s_rbac). Each ported body is a byte-for-byte copy of framework.v2.verify.oracles, pinned to the in-tree oracle on BOTH fired AND conclusive by integration/tests/test_general_reexecutable.py (an oracle-level battery + a dispatch SOUND/FORGE-A-FALSE harness over real retained evidence). HONEST BOUND (unchanged, same as posture): re-firing proves the verdict is the correct FUNCTION of the retained evidence, not that the evidence reflects the live target (a live re-run is still required for that). Re-execution is over RETAINED evidence, so a family whose LIVE capture needed a socket/browser/subprocess/cloud-API is still PURE at re-exec (it reads retained bytes); that is why the capture oracles are portable. What REMAINS genuinely IRREDUCIBLE is EXACTLY three oracles whose re-fire import-closure needs a module NOT in stdlib + cryptography — version_range (packaging), saml_forgery (signxml / lxml), and oob_callback (the framework verify.oob receipt-verification backing an EXTERNAL collector). These are NAMED here, never faked as reproduced; their re-verification rests on the signature + an in-VIGIL re-run (the sound maximum). The classification is enforced OBJECTIVELY by import-closure and PINNED by integration/tests/test_general_reexecutable.py::test_bucket_classification_is_enforced (_PORTED must be stdlib-closure and callable in verify_vf; _PURE_BUT_DEFERRED is now EMPTY; the irreducible set must be EXACTLY those three). This limitation is NOT claimed closed — the function-of-retained-evidence bound and the three-oracle irreducible boundary are named precisely.

limitations.title: single_engagement guard discards an empty engagement_slug
limitations.summary: A certificate with an empty engagement_slug can ride a named-engagement bundle without tripping the cross-engagement guard. Defense-in-depth only; it still requires a governance-signed head over the mixed chain. Deferred so uniform legacy empty-slug bundles under a named head keep verifying.

limitations.title: The evidence producer does not yet guarantee unique finding_refs
limitations.summary: The verifier refuses a bundle with duplicate finding_refs (closing a context-lookup collision), but the producer can still fall back to bug_class, so a legitimately-minted bundle with two same-class findings would be refused (fail-closed). Follow-up: key/emit unique refs at the producer.

limitations.title: The field record accrues only over real authorized engagements
limitations.summary: Deterministic-scanner recall is MEASURED (M1) on a planted loopback corpus; a genuine field record of finding real bugs on diverse authorized real targets is not manufacturable in a lab and this repo does not claim one exists. State the planted-corpus number and any field record separately; never word an accruing record as completeness.

limitations.title: The independent third-party audit needs an external team
limitations.summary: VIGIL prepares a reproducible, offline-verifiable audit package, but it cannot BE the independent third party. That conclusion is the external auditor's to write; it is a property of the world, not unfinished code.

limitations.title: Seal-at-capture is wired: credential excerpts on the append-only spine are sealed under the per-engagement DEK before they are written
limitations.summary: CLOSED (wave-a/waveA1-seal). Seal-at-capture is now wired at the single append-only writer: Blackboard.post seals ObservationPayload.raw_excerpt and ResultPayload.body_excerpt under the per-engagement DEK (crypto_shred.seal_excerpt) BEFORE the row is written, so a credential excerpt never reaches the spine in plaintext; every in-engagement reader unseals transparently (Blackboard.reveal_excerpt: hypothesis-agent, the console Live tailer, the tier-3 audit observation), and after a crypto-shred the excerpt is unrecoverable while the append-only row and the spine hash-chain stay byte-for-byte unchanged. Proven end-to-end (seal -> reveal -> shred) by engine/crucible/framework/v2/agents/tests/test_spine_seal_at_capture.py, alongside the existing evidence_dir shred proof in test_evidence_erasure.py. RESIDUALS (honest scope): (1) FindingPayload.oracle_context is retained in plaintext on the spine because framework.v2 verify re-fires over it offline; it is intentionally NOT sealed by this slice (sealing it would need a verify-path-aware unseal), so a credential reflected inside a retained proof remains plaintext and is tracked as a separate, narrower concern. (2) Only captures written AFTER this wiring are sealed; append-only rows written before it cannot be retroactively sealed without rewriting them (which would break tamper-evidence), so a legacy spine's pre-wiring excerpts remain as they were, while every fresh engagement is fully protected. (3) The console Live tailer opens its own Blackboard/keyring and reveals excerpts only when its evidence_keys_dir resolves to the same path as the engine's (the default in a single-host deployment); if an operator splits the keystore across the two processes, the Live view shows the redacted placeholder rather than plaintext -- a display-availability caveat, never a leak and never a crash.

limitations.title: Cloud / Kubernetes / infrastructure posture assessments record no structured findings or retained proofs
limitations.summary: The cloud, k8s and infra OperationTypes record only that a run happened and their own summary text; they do not yet write a structured findings record or retained proofs the way a web test does (records_findings=False, records_proofs=False). A deploying institution running these gets narrative output, not graded findings.

limitations.title: Container-level kill of the Strix sandbox is not wired into the VIGIL plane
limitations.summary: The vendored kill_run exists but has no VIGIL caller, so a force-remove of the sandbox container is honestly declared UNAVAILABLE in the console rather than shown as a working control. Orphaned containers are reaped at the next launch; the engagement kill-switch (halts the loop) and process-stop (ends the host pid) are the working controls.

limitations.title: The favicon-fingerprint table is an illustrative stub, not a crawled corpus
limitations.summary: _KNOWN_FAVICONS holds a handful of illustrative fixture entries so the fingerprint code path is real and deterministically testable; a production build would hash real product favicons from a crawled corpus. Because the table is a stub, favicon matches are scored conservatively and never mint a high-confidence technology fact.

limitations.title: The richer accessibility-tree capture path is a documented seam, not wired
limitations.summary: SIGIL perception captures the screen via a screenshot tool + OCR (grab_screen); the richer accessibility-tree path (C4) is a documented seam that is not wired, so on headless hosts with no screenshot tool grab_screen returns None rather than falling back to an a11y tree.

limitations.title: Native gesture/input injection on macOS and Windows is not wired (backend is honestly inert)
limitations.summary: SIGIL's gesture session injects input via a platform backend; the macOS/Windows native path is not wired (and Linux needs ydotool/xdotool). A backend whose available() is False is honestly INERT: it no-ops, and an injection is never recorded/returned as done when it physically did nothing.

limitations.title: The target-authorization owner anchor + trust root live under the offense-writable root
limitations.summary: Phase 1.c ties a UI-authorized target to the PINNED owner key AT INSTALL, and the launch gate verifies the authority against the on-disk trust root. Both the owner-pubkey anchor (the .vigil-live seam) and the persisted .authority-root trust root live, by default, under paths a full owner-uid filesystem-write actor could rewrite — such an actor could plant their own trust root + self-signed authority, and is outside the meaningful threat model (they could equally edit code, the kill-switch, or the keys). The install-time owner-pin raises the bar from 'write a plaintext charter' to 'produce an owner-signed authority whose trust root is the pinned owner key over the target host'. Closing even the full-FS-write case is a DEPLOYMENT choice (not unfinished code): anchor the launch-gate authority root out-of-band on a read-only / HSM-backed .authority-root mount via VIGIL_AUTHORITY_ROOT_DIR. This is now VISIBLE — `vigil doctor`'s authority-root-anchor posture line reports DEFAULT-IN-TREE vs OUT-OF-BAND — and DOCUMENTED in docs/runbooks/anchor-trust-root-out-of-band.md (incl. the caveat that the trust root must be CLI-provisioned before the mount is made read-only). The hard root pin (CRUCIBLE_ROOT_STRICT, claim PHASE1-5) additionally prevents a sentinel-less root from silently resolving elsewhere.

limitations.title: The deep/full engagement profile names packs wired incrementally across the FACT-coverage waves
limitations.summary: Wave 0.2 ships `--profile {surface,deep,full}` as additive-only flag expansion (resolve_profile), and the enable_* passes the roster flips (browser DOM/stored-XSS, SSO acceptance, GraphQL amplification; full adds the operator-spec access-control pack) were wired end-to-end into engage.py by slice 0.2 and the earlier waves that built each pass. Wave 6's diff does NOT touch engage.py: it added the benchmark-side profile mirror (_PROFILE_ROSTER) plus the corpus-wide zero-FP gate (zero_fp_gate) and fixed the browser DOM-XSS endpoint field, so the whole deep/full roster is now proven zero-FP corpus-wide. As of Wave 6 the deep/full rosters STILL name some packs that have no dedicated enable_* flag and so remain profile-deferred — deep names time-based / NoSQL / LDAP / XPath SQLi, full additionally names business-logic and race; _PROFILE_DEFERRED lists them. resolve_profile expands to NOTHING for a not-yet-wired name (it never invents a pack), and the profile manifest + an operator note surface the gap so it is visible and auditable. Wiring a dedicated profile enable_* flag (and any missing pack) for these remaining names is a later-wave item; the profile stays pure flag-expansion until then.

limitations.title: The DNS OOB collector records the RESOLVER's source IP, not the target's
limitations.summary: A blind DNS callback to <token>.<base-domain> reaches the authoritative DNS collector via the target's RECURSIVE RESOLVER, so the client_ip on the recorded OOBHit is the resolver's, not the target's. This is a property of DNS, not unfinished code. The FACT still holds because the correlator is the UNIQUE per-probe secret token (secrets.token_hex(16)) embedded in the callback host — a DNS query VIGIL did not cause cannot carry it — not the source IP. Documented on the oob_callback.dns_collector evidence branch and in ARCHITECTURE.md / OPERATOR-GUIDE.md.

limitations.title: The DNS OOB collector assumes an operator-owned domain whose NS delegate to it
limitations.summary: The authoritative DNS collector confirms a DNS-only interaction only when the base domain it serves is an operator-OWNED domain whose NS records delegate to the collector's public IP (UDP :53). This is a deployment assumption (own + delegate a domain), a property of the deployment rather than unfinished code; without the delegation, no target resolver forwards <token>.<base-domain> to us. The CLI serve-dns subcommand prints the exact NS-delegation instructions. Documented on the oob_callback.dns_collector evidence branch.

limitations.title: A DNS lookup proves resolution reached us, not that a full connection completed
limitations.summary: A fired DNS OOB FACT proves the target's resolver forwarded a token-bearing lookup to the authoritative collector — i.e. resolution reached us — NOT that a full HTTP (or other) connection then completed. This is a strictly weaker (but still sound) claim than the HTTP collaborator's completed-fetch proof, and a property of the DNS channel rather than unfinished code. It is exactly why DNS-only confirmation is valuable against a target that blocks outbound HTTP but still resolves. Documented on the oob_callback.dns_collector evidence branch.

limitations.title: A DNS OOB token is broadcast in cleartext, so token-only (VF-2a) is forgeable within the window
limitations.summary: A DNS out-of-band correlation token rides as a QNAME label, broadcast in cleartext to every recursive/forwarding resolver on the path and captured by passive-DNS, so token equality alone (VF-2a) does NOT prove the target emitted the lookup — anyone who observes the query can replay the label within the window. This is why a DNS OOB FACT REQUIRES the VF-2b independent-collector receipt (signed by an owner-pinned out-of-band key). Anti-replay for a receipt-bearing hit is bounded by the OWNER-SIGNED ENGAGEMENT WINDOW: the collector-signed, target-observed received_at must fall inside [not_before, not_after] (± skew) taken from the same signed EngagementAuthority as the pin, never from the producer context — this is NON-FORGEABLE and closes cross-engagement and gross-stale (e.g. year-1970 / prior-engagement) replay, and it cannot be slid because the producer cannot move an owner-signed window. (One precise corner: reusing the SAME owner-signed collector pin across two engagements whose authorized windows OVERLAP admits a receipt observed during the overlap in both — its signed received_at is temporally in-scope for each, so it degenerates into the intra-window residual below rather than a stale/out-of-scope replay; distinct collector pins or non-overlapping windows eliminate this corner.) The producer-recorded mint anchor issued_at is kept only as a best-effort intra-engagement freshness hint (it may narrow the window, never widen it, and is never the sole boundary); because the mint time is not cryptographically committed into the token, this is COARSE anti-replay: NOT tight anti-replay against a fully-dishonest producer WITHIN the window — a real receipt observed during the authorized window, re-presented later within the SAME window, remains indistinguishable. That residual is bounded to the owner-signed engagement window. The receipt + owner-signed window are what make the FACT sound, not token secrecy. A property of the DNS channel plus the uncommitted mint time, not unfinished code.

limitations.title: The legacy tls_breadth.classify_certificate_defects derivation is superseded and on no live path
limitations.summary: TLS certificate-validity classification IS now wired on the live path (M1.3, commit 98b33744): OracleKind.CERTIFICATE_VALIDITY / verify.oracles.certificate_validity_oracle adjudicates a presented leaf's validity defects (expired / not-yet-valid against a retained instant, hostname-mismatch, structural self-signed), captured by external_tool._tls_cert_capture and re-driven via the certificate_validity BUG_CLASS_ORACLES row, so evidence branch tls_weakness.certificate_validity is now wired:true / fact_capable:true and a minted FACT re-verifies offline. What remains is the OLDER derivation this entry anchors: tls_breadth.classify_certificate_defects re-derives the same defect set from the retained leaf, deterministically and offline against a retained capture instant, but M1.3 wired a SEPARATE oracle rather than this function. So classify_certificate_defects is reviewed and tested yet on no live path (this module stamps no captured_at_epoch and no re-drive calls it) — superseded legacy code. The three tls_breadth.py honest-limit docstrings this entry still covers continue to describe that FUNCTION as BUILT/TESTED/NOT WIRED, which remains true of the function itself even though the capability is now served by the new oracle. Future work (file-into-w16): remove or consolidate the superseded derivation and the now-stale claim-4 prose in tls_breadth.py, then retire this entry together with its remaining sites.

limitations.title: SIGIL sovereign-plane voice + credential-probe provider egress is sovereignty-tier-governed but not gateway-routed/redacted
limitations.summary: M4.1 routes the SIGIL sovereign plane's cloud LLM egress (frontier vision upload + cloud memory consolidation) through the shared chokepoint vigil_core.ai_gateway.egress (classify -> redact -> audit), and the no-bypass guard (integration/tests/test_egress_no_bypass_guard.py) now scans apps/sigil to enforce it. Two sovereign-plane provider-egress classes are NOT routed through that chokepoint: (1) the ElevenLabs VOICE provider (voice.backends.ElevenLabsTts.synth sends TTS text; ElevenLabsAsr.transcribe sends STT audio; find_voices does a voice-library lookup) and (2) the credential-validation probes (platform.secret_probes, which POST a candidate key to a provider's metadata endpoint to validate it). Both are governed by the SIGIL sovereignty tier (sigil.sovereignty.assert_endpoint_permitted — an air-gapped/sovereign tier REFUSES them before any socket opens) and are honestly out of the LLM-gateway's scope: voice is a distinct egress class (audio synthesis/recognition; STT carries no text prompt to redact; TTS speaks SIGIL's own already-governed responses), and a probe deliberately sends the credential itself to verify it (redaction cannot help). The residual gap vs. the LLM sites: their accompanying text is not symmetrically masked and they emit no unified ai_gateway audit record. Future work (file-into-w16, the recorded blocking_work): route ElevenLabsTts.synth's text through a voice-aware egress case (redact the text, let audio bytes pass like image bytes) and emit a unified audit record for the voice + probe egress. The local PiperTts / WhisperAsr backends remain the sovereign zero-egress alternative.

honest_limit_sites_note: The code-scan census. docs/tests/test_limitation_inventory.py scans every non-test product .py for the honest-limit/deferred debt phrases in _DEBT_PHRASES and requires EVERY hit to be either a VIGIL-LIMIT marker line OR a site listed here whose snippet (matched case-insensitively) is a substring of the hit line. kind 'debt' names the limitations id the site belongs to (which must exist); kind 'non-debt' explains why the phrase is not a capability limit (a deliberate design choice, a runtime-state description, or a phrase describing a CHECK's target rather than VIGIL itself). Bidirectional: every snippet here must still match a debt-phrase line in its file, so deleting the prose (or moving the debt) turns CI red.
